claims.text_en: BTS National Stadium (code W1) opened 5 December 1999 as the terminus of the Silom line's western branch, at 13.7465139 N, 100.5291083 E - identical to the app's unit center - on Rama I Road west of the Pathum Wan junction. The station's skybridge links directly to the National Stadium complex, MBK Center, Siam Discovery, the Bangkok Art and Culture Centre and Siam Square; the Jim Thompson House sits opposite in Soi Kasemsan 2, and Chulalongkorn University's sports-science and psychology faculties front the street level.

geography.place_name: BTS National Stadium station, Rama I Road
geography.notes: OSM node 11505460640 equals the app center.

evidence.paraphrase: W1, terminus toward Siam/Bang Wa direction, opened 5 Dec 1999, skybridge links to National Stadium/MBK/Siam Discovery/BACC/Siam Square, Jim Thompson House opposite in Soi Kasemsan 2, CU faculties at ground level.

claims.text_en: The station's namesake, Suphachalasai Stadium in the National Stadium complex (Wang Mai, Pathum Wan), was built 1937 and opened 1938, named after Luang Suphachalasai, the 'father of Thai sport'; it seats 19,793 (35,000 concert configuration), hosted the 1966/1970/1978 Asian Games as main stadium, and is owned by Chulalongkorn University with the Department of Physical Education as operator.

evidence.paraphrase: Built 1937, opened 1938, expanded 1941; named after Luang Suphachalasai; 19,793 seats; Asian Games main stadium 1966/1970/1978; CU-owned, DoPE-operated.

limitations: Current operating arrangement stated only in outline by the source

claims.text_en: The gym_sports=9 score has a dual mechanism this unit should be honest about: the verified sports anchor is a 19,793-seat public stadium plus a university sports-science faculty, while the app's gym layer counts fitness venues - the two are different amenities, and the app's method does not separate them. The stadium is not a drop-in gym; its track-and-field and match use is scheduled.

claims.text_en: Event rhythm is the unit's swing factor: the stadium's concert calendar runs large - Blackpink drew 66,211 across two nights (7-8 January 2023), Stray Kids 20,600 on 14 December 2024, and three more stadium-scale shows are booked into 2026 (Three Man Down 7-8 March, 50,000; Seventeen 14-15 March; Treasure 16 May). On event nights the campus-quiet unit absorbs tens of thousands; between events it reverts to student and commuter texture.

evidence.paraphrase: Blackpink Jan 2023 (66,211), Stray Kids Dec 2024 (20,600), Three Man Down Mar 2026 (50,000), Seventeen Mar 2026, Treasure May 2026.

limitations: 2026 shows are announced bookings; attendance figures are listed/estimated by the source

claims.text_en: MBK Center anchors the unit's west edge: opened 7 February 1985, ~2,000 shops across 8 floors at the Rama I x Phaya Thai corner, historically youth-led (half of 100,000+ daily visitors were young Thais in 2009), with Don Don Donki, a Tops supermarket and a 40-stall food court on the 6th floor feeding everyday errands.

claims.text_en: The Jim Thompson House museum - six relocated teak houses, most 19th-century and moved from Ayutthaya, assembled by the American who founded the Thai Silk Company in 1948 and vanished in Malaysia in 1967 - was built in 1959 at 6 Soi Kasemsan 2, one block from this station, and runs guided tours.

limitations: Admission/hours not stated in the source (guide mentions 100 baht)

claims.text_en: Chulalongkorn University Centenary Park - opened August 2017, designed by LANDPROCESS (Kotchakorn Voraakhom) with N7A, about 11 acres (~4.45 ha; a project PDF says 30 rai/~4.8 ha - the figures differ), with a 1.3 km bike-priority CU Promenade, Thailand's largest green roof (5,200 m2) and million-gallon-scale rain retention - is the green=9 candidate: its OSM centroid sits 955 m from the app center, so most of the park likely falls OUTSIDE the 800 m catchment with only its northern part inside (partial). The app's 4.3 ha in-unit figure implies nearly the whole park, which the centroid geometry does not support.

Weekend spillover from Siam Square reaches MBK's doors; the quiet is between events and north of Rama I, not in the retail blocks.

question_answers.notes: Identity: W1 branch terminus serving the National Stadium complex, MBK and the Jim Thompson House; app center equals the true station site.
Everyday experience: campus-adjacent shopping and food at MBK, student texture, event-night surges at the stadium.
Mechanisms: transport=10 from the skybridge-linked W1; vibe=10 from the Siam seam; gym_sports=9 from the stadium-faculty mix (flagged).
Counter-evidence: no quiet refuge from the Siam crush inside the retail blocks; event nights import the crush instead.
Rhythm: weekday student/commuter base, weekend Siam spillover, concert nights (incl. three 2026 bookings).
Walkability: skybridge spine to MBK/Discovery/BACC/Square; straight-line distances only, no radius-to-time conversions.
Daily life: MBK's Tops supermarket and food courts, street-level faculties, canal pier for the old town, cheaper rents than the neighbors.
36,500/82,000 is the batch's lowest blend; Wang Mai listing floor (12,900) supports the student-adjacent reading; still district-level, asking-basis.
Green=9 with 4.3 ha: Centenary Park is partial at best (centroid 955 m); the verified close-in green is two small parks; 4.3 ha needs the polygon.
Fit: students, MU-style event-goers, budget-leaning renters comfortable with weekend crush; poor fit for quiet-seekers on concert weekends.
2024-2026: event calendar verified; station-area infrastructure changes not found (gap).
Outside-the-score: gym-vs-venue method split, park-clip geometry, Scala-site redevelopment direction - flagged, unscored.

preview.text_en: The Silom line's western terminus in the shadow of a 19,793-seat national stadium: MBK's 2,000 stalls and food courts on one side, the Jim Thompson House teak compound on the other, and Centenary Park's green roof just past the catchment edge - with 66,000-person concert nights as the calendar's exclamation marks.

guide_lead.text_en: National Stadium is Siam's practical back door: same skywalk network, same food density in the app's top tier, but rents that start where the student khwaeng begins (app blend 36,500/82,000, the batch's lowest). The trade is precision - the stadium gives the unit its name and its event nights, and the park its green score leans on sits mostly beyond the 800-meter line.

strengths.text_en: Skybridge-connected everyday logistics: MBK (Tops supermarket, 40-stall food court, Don Don Donki) plus BACC and Siam Discovery on one covered spine from the W1 platform.
A real sports-and-culture anchor pair: a 19,793-seat national stadium with a packed 2024-2026 concert calendar, and the Jim Thompson House museum one block away.

tradeoffs.text_en: The green=9 figure outruns the geometry: Centenary Park's centroid is 955 m out, so only its northern tip likely sits inside; the verified close-in green is two small parks - the 4.3 ha claim needs the polygon to survive.
gym_sports=9 blends two different things: a scheduled-event stadium (not a drop-in gym) and the app's fitness-venue count - the score is defensible but the mechanism should be separated.
Event-night crush: bookings for 50,000-person shows in 2026 mean the unit's crowd experience can flip overnight without any change to its score.

day_night.text_en: Daytime runs on campus and MBK errands - food courts, phone stalls, faculty buildings; evenings lean on the Siam seam's food strip; concert nights (Dec 2024, Mar and May 2026 bookings) flood Rama I with tens of thousands, while non-event nights keep the hostel-and-student layer as the main late activity.

within_area_variation.text_en: The Rama I retail spine (MBK, Discovery, skybridge) is loud and continuous; north across the canal-side blocks toward Phetchaburi it thins to the Charoenpol pier lanes; east past Phaya Thai Road the campus gardens (Chamchuri 10) and pocket parks take over - three units of texture inside one scorecard.

conditional_fit.text_en: Fit for students, event-goers and budget-leaning renters who want Siam's food reach at the batch's lowest rent blend and can live with concert-night crowds.
Poor fit for quiet-seekers during event season and for anyone whose 'green' expectation is a large park inside the catchment - the flagship park sits mostly beyond the line.
